security_audit.summary: Static alerts describe Markdown syntax, scoped configuration reads, and intended XCrawl authentication rather than demonstrated malicious execution or exfiltration. Semantic review found documented TLS verification bypass defaults and a request-output contract that can expose supplied cookies or headers. No evidence found of prompt injection or malicious intent; provider behavior was not tested.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:139 documents skipped target TLS verification as the default.
remediation.suggestion: Explicitly set request.skip_tls_verification to false in examples and normal requests; require informed approval for exceptions.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:255-257 requires returning request payloads without excluding sensitive cookies or headers.
remediation.suggestion: Redact cookies, authorization headers, callback secrets, and sensitive URL parameters before displaying request payloads or storing diagnostic output.

content.user_title: Extract Web Page Data with XCrawl
content.value_statement: Web pages contain useful information in inconsistent formats. This skill guides XCrawl requests for selected formats and structured extraction while preserving upstream responses.
actual_capabilities: Guide single-page scrape requests through the XCrawl Scrape API.
Run synchronous requests or create asynchronous tasks and poll their results.
Select HTML, raw HTML, Markdown, links, summary, screenshot, or JSON output formats.
Describe structured extraction using a natural language prompt or JSON Schema.
Configure documented proxy locations, browser rendering, viewport settings, cookies, and request headers.
Configure asynchronous webhooks and return upstream responses with task identifiers, status, and available credit details.
limitations: Requires an XCrawl account, available credits, a local API key configuration, and curl or a compatible Node runtime.
Covers individual-page scraping; dedicated map, crawl, and search workflows are outside this skill.
Extraction quality and availability depend on XCrawl, target page behavior, and changing page structures.
Examples and parameter tables place JSON options differently; confirm the accepted request structure with the current API.

use_cases.title: Collect Research Sources
use_cases.description: Extract Markdown and links from selected public pages while preserving original responses for source review.

use_cases.title: Extract Product Attributes
use_cases.description: Request product titles and prices from authorized URLs, defining missing values and required fields before extraction.

use_cases.title: Integrate Asynchronous Scraping
use_cases.description: Create a scrape task, track its status, and inspect upstream results before integrating them into an application.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use XCrawl to extract Markdown from [public URL] synchronously. Keep TLS verification enabled and return the upstream response.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Multiple Formats
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch [public URL] with XCrawl and request Markdown plus links. Keep TLS verification enabled. Include task status and available credit usage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: select outputs and inspect task metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Defined Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract title, price, and currency from [authorized product URL] using XCrawl JSON extraction. Allow missing prices. Verify option placement and keep TLS verification enabled.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: define a structured extraction contract.

prompt_templates.title: Track an Asynchronous Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape [authorized URL] asynchronously with [JSON Schema]. Keep TLS verification enabled. Poll at reasonable intervals for at most two minutes. Redact sensitive payload fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: constrain polling and handle structured results.

output_examples.input: What should I expect from a synchronous Markdown and links request?
output: Illustrative output outline, not a live API result.
Endpoint and mode, followed by the request payload with sensitive values redacted.
The upstream response, including task status and requested content when available.
Available timestamps and credit usage, or error details if the request fails.

output_examples.input: How will an asynchronous product extraction report its progress?
output: Illustrative output outline, not a live API result.
The creation response supplies a task identifier and pending status.
Result requests can report pending, crawling, completed, or failed status.
A completed response includes extracted fields when available; a failed request includes upstream error details.

best_practices: Confirm URL scope, extraction fields, missing-value rules, and credit expectations before sending requests.
Explicitly enable target TLS verification and redact sensitive cookies, headers, and URL parameters from displayed payloads.
Keep credentials private, use explicit output formats, and apply reasonable polling intervals with a deadline.
anti_patterns: Using this single-page endpoint as a substitute for site discovery, site-wide crawling, or keyword search.
Sharing unrestricted request payloads containing session cookies, authorization headers, or webhook secrets.
Accepting disabled TLS verification or polling indefinitely without reviewing security and cost implications.

faq.question: What must I configure before using the skill?
faq.answer: Create ~/.xcrawl/config.json with your XCRAWL_API_KEY. You also need available XCrawl credits and curl or a compatible Node runtime.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Actual execution depends on the host allowing the required local file access and commands.

faq.question: Does this skill crawl an entire website?
faq.answer: No. It targets individual pages through XCrawl Scrape and directs map, crawl, or search requests toward dedicated APIs.

faq.question: Which output formats are documented?
faq.answer: The skill lists HTML, raw HTML, Markdown, links, summary, screenshot, and JSON. Returned fields depend on requested formats and API behavior.

faq.question: Are requests free?
faq.answer: XCrawl requests consume credits. The skill mentions a free credit plan, but current eligibility and pricing require confirmation with XCrawl.

faq.question: What security precautions are necessary?
faq.answer: Keep target TLS verification enabled, protect the local configuration file, and redact sensitive request payload fields before sharing results.
